arguments.arg1_rdi: out status struct (caller-provided). Entry copy writes u32 at +0, u16 at +4, pointer at +8. Short-path copy writes u16 at +0, u8 at +2, u16 at +3, u8 at +5, pointer at +8 (old pointer freed). Long path zeroes u32 at +0, u16 at +4, pointer at +8 (old pointer freed). The low byte at +0 gates reader construction and the arg5 rule.
arguments.arg2_rsi: context struct (kept in r13). Fields used: +0xa0 (stored to the reader pair slot), +0xa8/+0xb0 (entry-call object pair), +0x158/+0x160 (16 bytes copied to state +0x20), and the object at +0 (its +0x30 block is the reader-options source).
arguments.arg3_rdx: filename string object. Copied into state +0x10; its basename (after the last '/' or '\') goes into state +0x60/+0x68/+0x70.
arguments.arg4_rcx: passed unchanged as r9 to the WAL reader constructor.
arguments.arg5_r8: out pointer (u64 slot). Written on every path except the arg1-gate path: 0 or 1 by the teardown rule, or the first 8 bytes of the applied record on the long path.

basename.overflow: if position > length, the substr out-of-range throw fires (format at 0x7d66e0)
basename.rule: find_last_of(charset) on the filename; position = found + 1; substring (position, length - position) is the basename

callers.note: census by whole-file e8 scan (site vaddr = file offset + 0x1000), e9 scan, and qword scan; both call sites encode e8 to 0x520ad30 (see caller-site excerpts)

cf_filter.append: kept pairs (element pointer, reference field) are appended to the state +0x88 vector in walk order; the vector grows through 0x4fa5eb0 when full
cf_filter.input: the (begin, end) element vector in the -0x210/-0x208 slots, stride 0x10 (element pointer at +0, reference field at +8)
cf_filter.keep_rule: keep an element only when its vtable +0x140 method differs from 0x4fa4610 AND that method, called on the element, returns nonzero
cf_filter.release: after filtering, every input element is released (decrement; destroy via 0x4f94a40 on last release) and the input vector buffer is freed

entry_calls.entry_shared_ptr_traffic: the context +0xb0/+0xa8 objects are reference-counted (increment on copy, decrement with destroy-on-last-release via 0x4f94a40); the exact atomic vs plain variant follows a global flag at 0x5777ed8. Mechanics are described generically, not byte-pinned.
entry_calls.first_virtual: vtable offset 0x188 of the context +0xa8 object's vtable, called with (stack slot -0x210, the +0xa8 object, context + 8). The -0x210/-0x208 slots afterwards hold the (begin, end) element vector walked by the filter loop. Internals are a callee contract.
entry_calls.second_virtual: vtable offset 0xa8 of the same object's vtable, called with (scratch -0x220, the +0xa8 object, the filename string, the -0x210 slot, the -0x268 slot, 0). It fills the -0x220 scratch status, which is then copied into arg1 out (u32 at +0, u16 at +4, pointer at +8). Internals are a callee contract.

gate.condition: byte at arg1 out +0 is nonzero, checked after the input vector is released
gate.effect: jump straight to the state teardown (0x520b6f6); the reader is never constructed and arg5 is never written

long_path.after: the record-state object is reset via 0x52178b0, then reader destroy and state teardown (the teardown rule is skipped on this path)
long_path.apply: 0x521cbf0(out scratch at &-0x220, record-state object, record slice at -0x250): replaces the record-state +0x40 string with the record bytes, sets record-state +0x24 to 1, zeroes the out scratch (u32 at +0, u16 at +4, pointer at +8)
long_path.arg5: 0x521b610(record-state object) returns the first qword of the record-state +0x40 string data, i.e. the first 8 bytes of the record; stored into arg5
long_path.out_move: the (now zeroed) scratch is moved into arg1 out (u32 at +0, u16 at +4, pointer at +8), freeing the old out +8 buffer; the scratch fields are zeroed as they are moved

record_read.accumulator_initial: stack string with inline buffer at -0x160, length 0
record_read.after: record length is the out slice length at -0x248; success is a nonzero return
record_read.call: 0x51618e0(reader, out slice at -0x250, accumulator string at -0x170, mode 0, null transform)

short_path.detail: 0x542f040(status at -0x220, code 2, message slice 'log record too small' length 0x14 at 0x1e32ac, plus the record slice)
short_path.format: 0x542f8a0(formatted string at -0x150, status at -0x220). The formatted text is a callee contract; the packet pins the call and its inputs, not the rendered text.

state_object.plus_0x00: address of its own +0x10 field (sentinel-style self pointer)
state_object.plus_0x10: string copy of the filename (SSO inline, heap via _M_create over 15 bytes)
state_object.plus_0x30: static base 0x575f690 + 0x10, restored to the same value during teardown
state_object.plus_0x58: first qword of the singleton object returned by 0x5242050
state_object.plus_0x60: basename string: pointer at +0x60, length at +0x68, inline buffer at +0x70 (heap via _M_create over 15 bytes, NUL at buffer + length)

status_field_copy.condition: short path only, when arg1 out byte is 0
status_field_copy.skip: when arg1 out byte is nonzero, the copy is skipped and the old scratch pointer buffer is freed instead
status_field_copy.writes: u16 from scratch -0x220 to out +0; u8 from scratch -0x21e to out +2; u16 from scratch -0x21d to out +3; u8 from scratch -0x21b to out +5; pointer from scratch -0x218 to out +8 (the old out +8 buffer is freed first when nonzero; the record string is copied into out +8's buffer through 0x542efe0 when the scratch pointer is nonzero)

teardown_rule.arg5_skip: the gate path and the long path do not run this rule (gate path writes nothing; long path writes the record head instead)
teardown_rule.arg5_value: 1 if and only if the out byte read at rule time is 0 AND flag byte at -0x7f is 0 AND flag byte at -0x7d is nonzero; otherwise 0. On the short path the out byte read here is the POST-copy byte: the status field copy overwrites out +0 with the scratch u16's low byte, so a nonzero scratch low byte forces 0 even when both flags are set for 1. The producers of the -0x7f/-0x7d flags are not pinned (they sit in the reader-adjacent stack slots); the rule itself is pinned by the branch structure at 0x520b690-0x520bbf0.
order: accumulator string disposed (heap buffer freed when the stored pointer differs from the saved inline-buffer address)
